bds.h: U.S. army says detonation of bomb chemicals in Iowa a success despite toxic plume concerns
bds.lede: The U.S. Army intentionally blew up the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, in southeastern Iowa on Wednesday after officials said the five tons of material had degraded and were at risk of exploding uncontrollably as temperatures cooled.
rows: The Army detonated five tons of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, and FEMA says residents within 20 miles must shelter until the all clear.
Despite widespread concern from residents ahead of the blast, officials say that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.
Army hails Iowa's lead azide disposal operation as some experts warn of potentially hidden toxins.
Maps released by the Army Tuesday show a possible plume of toxic dust after its detonation of munitions in Iowa drifting southwest toward northeast Missouri between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Wednesday.
